desc:
Beads of various colors are strung on a closed necklace: colors[i] is the color of bead i, and bead n - 1 is next to bead 0. Pick a run of consecutive beads, which may wrap around the end of the array, so that the run contains every color that appears on the necklace.

Return the smallest possible number of beads in such a run.

colors = [1, 2, 2, 1, 3, 3, 1]
colors present: 1, 2, 3
beads 2..4 = [2, 1, 3] contain all three colors, and no run of 2 beads does
result = 3
hints: Without the wrap-around this is the classic 'shortest subarray containing all distinct values'. How could you reuse that solution?
A run that wraps around the end of the array is a normal subarray of the array written twice (colors + colors).

Slide a window over the doubled array with a count map and a counter of covered colors. Shrink from the left while everything is covered, tracking the minimum length. The best length is never more than n, so no window needs to be longer.
editorial: Cutting the necklace open at a different place only changes where the array starts, so every circular run corresponds to a plain subarray of the doubled array colors + colors with length at most n. The task becomes: find the shortest window of the doubled array containing all D different colors.

Use the usual two-pointer technique: add arr[right] to a count map, and while the number of colors with a positive count equals D record the window length and remove arr[left]. Any n consecutive beads cover every color, so the answer is at most n and starting the answer at n is safe. The doubled array has 2n elements, so the time is O(n) and the extra space O(n).
solution:
def shortestCircularCover(colors):
    n = len(colors)
    need = len(set(colors))
    arr = colors + colors
    cnt = {}
    have = 0
    left = 0
    best = n
    for right in range(2 * n):
        x = arr[right]
        cnt[x] = cnt.get(x, 0) + 1
        if cnt[x] == 1:
            have += 1
        while have == need:
            best = min(best, right - left + 1)
            y = arr[left]
            cnt[y] -= 1
            if cnt[y] == 0:
                have -= 1
            left += 1
    return best
